<objective>
Make the password-reset "choose a new password" stage reachable only from a redeemed
recovery link (CR-03), remove the attacker-controlled header from the reset redirect
(WR-04), require re-authentication for password changes (WR-14), and make the signup
consent path recoverable and honest (WR-07, WR-02, WR-03).

**As a** restaurant owner who left the shared tablet unlocked, **I want to** know that
nobody who walks up to it can change my password, **so that** a momentary lapse of
physical custody is not a permanent account takeover.

Purpose: today `/reset-password?stage=set` renders the change-password form for anyone who
types the URL, and `completePasswordReset` accepts any live `getUser()` result with
`secure_password_change = false`. That is a full account-takeover primitive for anyone who
reaches a live owner session — and the D-07 owner-unlocked shared tablet is exactly that
state, by design. The page's own comment claims a protection that does not exist at either
layer.

Output: a server-held, signed, user-bound recovery grant; a pure origin resolver; a
tightened GoTrue config; and three new test files.
</objective>

  <action>
    Create `lib/recovery-session.ts`, mirroring the structure of `lib/staff-session.ts` and
    importing nothing from `next/*` so it stays Vitest-reachable. Export:

    - `RECOVERY_COOKIE_NAME` = the string `cena_recovery`.
    - `RECOVERY_GRANT_TTL_SECONDS` = 900. Fifteen minutes: long enough to choose and type a
      password, short enough that a grant left behind on a shared tablet is worthless.
    - `type RecoveryGrant = { userId: string; expiresAt: number }`.
    - `encodeRecoveryGrant(grant: RecoveryGrant): string` — build the payload as the literal
      prefix `recovery` joined by `.` with `userId` and `expiresAt`, then append `.` and the
      hex HMAC-SHA256 of that payload. The prefix is a domain tag: this module is new, so it
      is built with type separation from the start rather than inheriting the untagged shape
      of the two existing cookies.
    - `decodeRecoveryGrant(value: string | undefined, nowSeconds?: number): RecoveryGrant | null`
      — split into exactly 4 parts, require part 0 to equal the literal prefix, verify the
      signature with `timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, require a finite `expiresAt`
      strictly greater than `nowSeconds` (default `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)`), and
      return null on any failure.
    - `assertRecoveryGrant(value: string | undefined, sessionUserId: string, nowSeconds?: number): boolean`
      — decode, then return whether the decoded `userId` strictly equals `sessionUserId`.
      Binding the grant to the user is what stops a grant minted for one account
      authorising a password change on another.

    Reuse the `STAFF_SESSION_SECRET ?? SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` fallback and throw with an
    actionable message when neither is set, exactly as the two existing codecs do.

    In `app/auth/confirm/route.ts`: after `redeemed` is true and before the final redirect,
    call `supabase.auth.getUser()`, and when a user comes back, write the grant cookie with
    `cookies()` from `next/headers` — `httpOnly: true`, `sameSite: "lax"`,
    `path: PASSWORD_RESET_PATH`, `secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"`,
    `maxAge: RECOVERY_GRANT_TTL_SECONDS`. Scoping `path` to the reset route means the cookie
    is not attached to any other request. Setting a cookie then redirecting in the same
    handler is the pattern `enableStaffMode` already relies on; keep the existing
    `redirect()` call rather than switching to `NextResponse`.

    Delete the stage-parameter mechanism entirely — it is a security-looking flag with no
    security in it, and leaving it beside the real gate creates two sources of truth. Remove
    `PASSWORD_RESET_STAGE_PARAM` and `PASSWORD_RESET_STAGE_SET` from `lib/validation/auth.ts`
    and from `app/auth/confirm/route.ts`, and run `grep -rn PASSWORD_RESET_STAGE` across the
    repo to find and update every remaining importer.

    In `app/(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx`: replace the `setStage` derivation with a read of
    `cookies()` for `RECOVERY_COOKIE_NAME` passed through `decodeRecoveryGrant`. A Server
    Component may READ cookies during render (it may not write them), so this needs no

  <action>
    Create `lib/site-origin.ts` exporting
    `resolveSiteOrigin(options: { siteUrl?: string; nodeEnv?: string }): string`. Take both
    values as parameters rather than reading `process.env` inside, so the function is
    exhaustively testable without mutating the worker environment. Order: when `siteUrl` is
    a non-empty string after trimming, return it with one trailing slash removed; else when
    `nodeEnv` equals the literal `production`, throw an Error whose message names
    `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` and states that the reset redirect must never be derived from a
    request header; else return the literal `http://127.0.0.1:3000`. Export the development
    fallback as a named constant so the test asserts against the constant rather than a
    duplicated string.

    In `actions/auth.ts`, delete `requestOrigin` entirely and call
    `resolveSiteOrigin({ siteUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, nodeEnv: process.env.NODE_ENV })`
    at the single use site in `requestPasswordReset`. This removes both halves of WR-04 at
    once: the `x-forwarded-host` read that lets a client choose the origin, and the
    `startsWith` protocol sniff that downgrades a host like `localhost.attacker.example` to
    plain http. Remove the now-unused `headers` import from `next/headers` if nothing else in
    the file uses it — check with grep before deleting.

    Keep `requestPasswordReset`'s uniform-response property exactly as it is. The existing
    guard-rail comment above it forbids adding an error branch; a thrown origin error would
    become one. Because the throw can only fire in production with the variable unset, and
    because that is a deployment misconfiguration rather than a per-request condition, let it
    propagate rather than catching it — a deployment that cannot build a valid reset link
    should fail loudly at the first reset request, not email a poisoned one.

    In `.env.example`, replace the empty `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=` line with a comment block
    stating that it is optional in development and REQUIRED in production, that the reset
    redirect is built from it, and that leaving it unset in production is a hard error rather
    than a fallback.

    Create `tests/lib/site-origin.test.ts` covering every case in `&lt;behavior&gt;`. Write the
    production-throw case first and confirm it fails against the current header-derived
    implementation.
  </action>

    - terms_accepted_at read back after the second call is unchanged from after the first.

  <action>
    **WR-07 — make the stranded state recoverable.** In `signUpOwner`, the `signUp()` call
    succeeds first and hands the browser a live session; if the subsequent `ensure_account`
    RPC then fails, the owner holds a session with no `accounts` row and the form can only
    ever fail again, because re-submitting calls `signUp()` with an email that now exists.
    Two changes:

    - On a non-null `consentError`, retry the RPC once against the same session before
      returning. Retrying the consent write is safe because `ensure_account` is idempotent by
      construction. Only return `COPY.errors.generic` when the retry also fails.
    - On a non-null `signUpError`, before returning the error, call `supabase.auth.getUser()`.
      When it returns a user whose email equals the submitted email, this is a re-submit
      after a failed consent write rather than a genuine duplicate-registration attempt — fall
      through to the `ensure_account` call instead of returning. When there is no such user,
      keep returning `COPY.errors.auth` unchanged, because that path is the
      account-enumeration boundary and must stay uniform.

    Add a comment recording why the fall-through is not an enumeration leak: it fires only
    when the caller already holds a session for that address, which they can only have by
    having just created it.

    **WR-02 — make the comment match the SQL.** The JSDoc on `ensureAccount` says the RPC
    upserts and refreshes the accepted version. It does not; migration 0001 uses
    `on conflict (owner_user_id) do nothing`, and its own SQL comment correctly says the
    first accepted version is the one on record. Do NOT change the SQL. Silently restamping
    an owner's consent with a version string they were never shown would record consent that
    did not happen — the same class of defect as CR-04 pointed the other way — and honest
    re-consent needs a UI this phase does not have. Rewrite the JSDoc to state the actual
    semantics: idempotent, first accepted version wins, no consent history in v1, and a
    Terms bump requires a re-consent flow that is deliberately not built yet. Record the
    re-consent flow as a forward item in the plan summary.

    **WR-03 — delete the claim, keep the honest residual.** The header comment in
    `GoogleOneTap.tsx` asserts that ticking the consent checkbox is what allows the One Tap
    prompt to initialise, and therefore that consent precedes the session. That is true of
    the UI and false of the boundary: `ensureAccount` is an exported Server Action reachable
    by direct POST, and the version it compares against is a constant already present in the
    client bundle. Remove that assertion from the comment and replace it with a statement of
    what the checkbox actually does (orders the UI) and what it does not (constitute
    server-held evidence). In `actions/auth.ts`, extend the `ensureAccount` JSDoc to record
    the residual explicitly: any caller holding a session can stamp a valid-looking consent
    row, the version check stops only a client choosing its own wording, and closing this
    properly requires a server-issued "terms presented" token, which is deferred. An
    accurate comment about a real residual is worth more than a reassuring one about a
    protection that does not exist.

    Create `tests/auth/consent-evidence.test.ts` covering every case in `&lt;behavior&gt;`. Sign
    owners in through the anon key with `createOwnerUser` + `signIn`, call the
    `ensure_account` RPC directly through those anon-key clients, and read
    `terms_accepted_version` and `terms_accepted_at` back through `typedAdmin` as a
    ground-truth re-read (never as an authorization assertion — that is the `tests/rls/setup.ts`
    rule). Register users for teardown and call `cleanupUsers()` in `afterAll`.
  </action>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| emailed link -> `app/auth/confirm/route.ts` | An attacker-influenced URL arrives pre-trusted in the owner's inbox; the token is redeemed server-side here. |
| browser -> `completePasswordReset` | A live session crosses into a password write. On the D-07 shared tablet, that session is deliberately an owner's. |
| request headers -> outbound reset email | Any value used to build `redirectTo` becomes a link a human is trained to click. |
| browser -> `ensureAccount` Server Action | An exported Server Action reachable by direct POST writes GDPR consent evidence. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01G-07 | Elevation of Privilege | `app/(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx` + `completePasswordReset` | critical | mitigate | CR-03: the recovery gate is a client-supplied query parameter and the action accepts any live session, giving full account takeover from an unattended owner-unlocked tablet. Task 1 replaces both with a signed, user-bound, path-scoped, 15-minute grant that only the confirm route can mint, deletes it on success, and sets `secure_password_change = true` so GoTrue independently requires re-authentication. Proven closed by `assertRecoveryGrant` returning false for a wrong-user grant and for an absent grant. |
| T-01G-08 | Spoofing | `requestOrigin` in `actions/auth.ts` | high | mitigate | WR-04: reset-link poisoning via `x-forwarded-host`, plus a protocol downgrade for hosts matching the `startsWith` sniff. Task 2 removes header reads entirely; production without `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` throws rather than falling back. |
| T-01G-09 | Tampering | recovery grant cookie | medium | mitigate | A forged grant must not authorise a password change. HMAC-SHA256 with `timingSafeEqual`, a domain prefix, a hard expiry compared against an injectable clock, and a strict equality check against the session's own user id. All six failure modes are asserted in Task 1. |
| T-01G-10 | Repudiation | `ensureAccount` consent evidence | medium | accept | WR-03: any session-holder can POST the action with the constant and stamp a valid-looking consent row. Accepted at ASVS L1 for this phase: the caller must already hold a session, and the harm is a weaker consent record rather than account compromise. Closing it needs a server-issued "terms presented" token, which is deferred. The false claim that the checkbox gates this is removed so no future reader relies on it. |
| T-01G-11 | Repudiation | `ensure_account` version semantics | medium | mitigate | WR-02: the calling JSDoc claims a refresh the SQL does not perform, so a Terms bump silently leaves every existing owner on the old string with nothing noticing. Task 3 makes the comment true and pins first-version-wins with a test that reads the column back. Deliberately NOT "fixed" by restamping, which would record consent to unseen terms. |
| T-01G-12 | Denial of Service | `signUpOwner` consent failure | medium | mitigate | WR-07: a failed consent RPC strands the owner with a session, no account row, and a form that can only fail. Task 3 retries the RPC and falls through on a re-submit that already holds a session for that address. |
| T-01G-13 | Information Disclosure | `signUpOwner` fall-through branch | low | mitigate | The new fall-through must not become an account-enumeration oracle. It fires only when `getUser()` already returns a session for the submitted address, which the caller can only hold by having just created it; every other path keeps the single shared `COPY.errors.auth` string. |
| T-01G-14 | Denial of Service | `secure_password_change = true` | medium | mitigate | Tightening the flag could break the legitimate recovery journey. Task 1 keeps `tests/auth/login-reset.test.ts` green as a gate and additionally re-drives the full mailbox-to-new-password journey under the new flag. |
</threat_model>
